new_or_changed_cards.support_text: To confirm that ROS contributes to azacytidine-induced cell necrosis, an Image-iT LIVE Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) Kit was used to detect ROS in untreated and azacytidine-treated U266 myeloma cells. Cells were labeled with carboxy-H2DCFDA, which fluoresces when oxidized by ROS, and nuclei were stained with blue-fluorescent Hoechst 33342. The azacytidine-treated cells exhibited much stronger green fluorescence (Figure 2e) compared to untreated cells (Figure 2d), indicating that azacytidine induced a significant increase in ROS.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: assay_format=imaging_or_morphometry | biological_system_context=Cryopreserved human primary hepatocytes (cryoheps, lot HC3-30), sandwich-cultured in Long-Term medium for 10 d from the next day after seeding and then in CDI maintenance medium (CM medium) for 5 d; intrinsically metabolically competent primary hepatocytes.

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: tested_entity_form=parent | probe_or_analyte=bile canaliculi (CDFDFA fluorescence and anti-BSEP immunostaining) | exposure_conditions=2',5'-Dideoxyadenosine (AMPK inhibitor) added during the 5 d culture on the CM medium; test concentration not reported in the extracted text. | extra_details=2',5'-Dideoxyadenosine is described in the paper as an AMP inhibitor. Test rationale: taurocholate activates AMPK and extends bile canaliculi (Fu et al. 2011, cited). Canalicular readout by CDFDA assay and immunostaining; bar graph gives average area of each bile canaliculus stained by anti-BSEP, means ± SD (n=3). The paper did not report a numeric area/length value. The original article calls 2-prime,5-prime-dideoxyadenosine an AMPK inhibitor. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Because taurocholate activates AMPK and extends the bile canaliculi (Fu et al. 2011), the effect on bile canaliculi formation was examined by adding 2',5'-dideoxyadenosine, an AMPK inhibitor, to the CM medium. This shortened the length of the bile canaliculi (Fig. 6d and e). The canaliculi were observed using the CDFDA assay and by immunostaining, and the bar graph shows the average area of each bile canaliculus stained by anti-BSEP, presented as means ± SD (n=3).

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: concentration_values=2 | concentration_unit=umol_per_l | exposure_duration_and_schedule=reconditioning exposure to 2 uM 5-AZA for 12 days; total RNA extracted after 3 and 5 days of culture without 5-AZA (T1 and T2) | exposure_regimen=repeated_dose_with_recovery | extra_details=Phenotype named: restoration of hepatocyte differentiation markers (differentiated-function/reserve endpoint). new_or_changed_cards.support_text: We analyzed the expression of a cluster of characteristic hepatospecific genes: albumin (ALB), solute carrier family 10 member 1 (SLC10A1), cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4, and microRNA-122 (miR-122). After epigenetic reconditioning of HepG2 and Hep3B cells with 2 μM 5-AZA for 12 days, qRT-PCR data revealed that these genes were significantly induced, indicating a restoration of hepatic differentiation in the reconditioned HCC cells. miR-122 levels were strongly increased in the reconditioned cells (p < 0.001); there was an apparent absence of ALB induction in reconditioned Hep3B cells, but ALB was already elevated in non-reconditioned Hep3B cells.

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: agent_type=small_molecule_or_chemical | liver_injury_identifier=UMLS:C0267797 | qualifying_conditions=The paper notes adverse hepatic reactions may occur more commonly in elderly patients with malignant disease treated with prolonged high doses; continuing the drug during the prodrome greatly increases severity and mortality. | extra_details=Latency about 2-3 months; prodromal non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) for 1-4 weeks before jaundice. Used in antiandrogenic conditions, recommended dose 2-300 mg daily (Androcur, Cyprostat). Figure shows serum total bilirubin and aspartate aminotransferase from withdrawal (day 0) to normalization of liver function tests; liver function monitoring recommended. Isoniazid and methyldopa mentioned only as analogous hepatotoxic drugs, not attributed as culprits in this case. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: This case describes drug-induced acute hepatitis caused by cyproterone acetate, with features similar to acute hepatitis from isoniazid and methyldopa: after about two to three months of treatment, non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) develop for one to four weeks before the onset of jaundice; severity and mortality increase greatly if the drug is continued during the prodrome. The toxicity of cyproterone acetate may be direct but is more likely the result of an idiosyncratic reaction caused by one of its metabolites, and an immunological mechanism has not been excluded.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: We analyzed the expression of a cluster of characteristic hepatospecific genes: albumin (ALB), solute carrier family 10 member 1 (SLC10A1), cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4, and microRNA-122 (miR-122). After epigenetic reconditioning of HepG2 and Hep3B cells with 2 μM 5-AZA for 12 days, qRT-PCR data revealed that these genes were significantly induced, indicating a restoration of hepatic differentiation in the reconditioned HCC cells. miR-122 levels were strongly increased in the reconditioned cells (p < 0.001); there was an apparent absence of ALB induction in reconditioned Hep3B cells, but ALB was already elevated in non-reconditioned Hep3B cells.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes, AICAR, which activates AMPK, circumvented the inhibitory effect of kinase-dead LKB1 constructs on canalicular network formation. Canalicular network formation was assessed by immunostaining for the apical protein ABCB1 and the tight junction marker occludin. Because AICAR restored canalicular formation despite kinase-dead LKB1, the authors conclude AMPK directly affects canalicular network formation.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: To elucidate the mechanism of KD's amelioration of EE-induced cholestasis, expression levels of BSEP, NTCP, CYP7A1 and SULT2A1 in rat liver were determined by Western blotting. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes, AICAR, which activates AMPK, circumvented the inhibitory effect of kinase-dead LKB1 constructs on canalicular network formation. Because AICAR restored canalicular formation despite kinase-dead LKB1, the authors conclude AMPK directly affects canalicular network formation.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes, AICAR, which activates AMPK, circumvented the inhibitory effect of kinase-dead LKB1 constructs on canalicular network formation. Canalicular network formation was assessed by immunostaining for the apical protein ABCB1 and the tight junction marker occludin. Because AICAR restored canalicular formation despite kinase-dead LKB1, the authors conclude AMPK directly affects canalicular network formation.

new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: clinical_phenotype=acute_hepatitis
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: agent_type=small_molecule_or_chemical | liver_injury_identifier=UMLS:C0267797 | qualifying_conditions=The paper notes adverse hepatic reactions may occur more commonly in elderly patients with malignant disease treated with prolonged high doses; continuing the drug during the prodrome greatly increases severity and mortality. | extra_details=Latency about 2-3 months; prodromal non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) for 1-4 weeks before jaundice. Mechanism uncertain, may be direct but more likely idiosyncratic via a metabolite; immunologic mechanism not excluded. Used in antiandrogenic conditions, recommended dose 2-300 mg daily (Androcur, Cyprostat). Figure shows serum total bilirubin and aspartate aminotransferase from withdrawal (day 0) to normalization of liver function tests; liver function monitoring recommended. Isoniazid and methyldopa mentioned only as analogous hepatotoxic drugs, not attributed as culprits in this case. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: This case describes drug-induced acute hepatitis caused by cyproterone acetate, with features similar to acute hepatitis from isoniazid and methyldopa: after about two to three months of treatment, non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) develop for one to four weeks before the onset of jaundice; severity and mortality increase greatly if the drug is continued during the prodrome. The toxicity of cyproterone acetate may be direct but is more likely the result of an idiosyncratic reaction caused by one of its metabolites, and an immunological mechanism has not been excluded.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: To test the link between SAM and PEMT in LRH-1 target gene expression, the authors treated cells with 3-Deazaadenosine (DZA), a specific inhibitor of PEMT enzymatic activity, and with a high dose acute homocysteine treatment that disrupts SAM-to-SAH flow. Expression of several other LRH-1 target genes, including Apoa1, Scarb1, Gls2 and Mdr3, was also reduced upon DZA or homocysteine treatment.

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: tested_entity_form=other_defined_test_article | probe_or_analyte=Mdr3 mRNA | exposure_conditions=3-Deazaadenosine (DZA) treatment to inhibit PEMT activity; concentration and duration not reported | extra_details=Paper's own name: 3-Deazaadenosine (DZA), a specific inhibitor of PEMT enzymatic activity. MDR3 (Abcb4) is a canalicular phospholipid translocator under the SAM-PEMT-LRH-1 axis. DZA/homocysteine also reduced other LRH-1 target genes (Cyp8b1, Shp, Apoa1, Scarb1, Gls2); only the Mdr3 (named hepatobiliary transporter) result is extracted here. LRH-1 transactivation reflects LRH-1, not FXR, and is not extracted. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: To test the link between SAM and PEMT in LRH-1 target gene expression, the authors treated cells with 3-Deazaadenosine (DZA), a specific inhibitor of PEMT enzymatic activity, and with a high dose acute homocysteine treatment that disrupts SAM-to-SAH flow. Both DZA and acute homocysteine treatments decreased mRNA expression of Lrh-1 target genes including Cyp8b1 and Shp, and reduced LRH-1 Gal4-LBD luciferase reporter activity. Expression of several other LRH-1 target genes, including Apoa1, Scarb1, Gls2 and Mdr3, was also reduced upon DZA or homocysteine treatment.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: experimental_system=in vitro, mouse bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs, primary cells) stimulated with IFN-γ/LPS | analytical_platform_and_normalization=real-time PCR
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: assay_family=targeted_gene_expression | endpoint_and_comparator=Nos2, Tnf, Il6, Il1b mRNA expression relative to untreated/vehicle, testing molecule-amplified inflammatory gene induction in the presence of IFN-γ/LPS challenge
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: immune_stimulus_regimen=IFN-γ/LPS | exposure_schedule=BMDMs co-treated with UDPG (dose series 0, 100, 200 μM) and IFN-γ/LPS for 24 or 36 h; sampling at 24/36 h | extra_details=Dose-response (100, 200 μM) reported collectively without dose-specific values; n=3 biologically independent experiments, mean±SEM, one-way ANOVA, **p<0.01, ****p<0.0001. Glucose is the glucopyranose donor, not the previously attached furanose isomer. Macrophage immune-signaling mechanism; no direct hepatic outcome is inferred. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: IFN-γ/LPS-stimulated BMDMs were treated with UDPG (0, 100 or 200 μM) for 24 or 36 h; Nos2, Tnf, Il6, and Il1b expression was determined by real-time PCR, and iNOS, TNF and IL-6 expression was determined by western blot and ELISA. Exogenous UDPG amplified the IFN-γ/LPS-driven inflammatory phenotype.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: experimental_system=in vitro, mouse BMDMs (primary), GPI or Pygl-siRNA treated, IFN-γ/LPS stimulated | analytical_platform_and_normalization=western blot (and two-photon confocal microscopy for nuclear translocation)
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: assay_family=protein_signaling_or_enzyme_activity | endpoint_and_comparator=STAT1 phosphorylation at Tyr701 and nuclear translocation relative to GPI/Pygl-inhibited IFN-γ/LPS-stimulated cells, testing UDPG-mediated restoration of STAT1 activation
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: immune_stimulus_regimen=IFN-γ/LPS | exposure_schedule=BMDMs pretreated with GPI (20 or 50 μM) for 30 min or pretransfected with Pygl siRNA for 24 h, then stimulated with IFN-γ/LPS with or without added UDPG; western blot of STAT1 phosphorylation from 15 to 120 min after stimulation | extra_details=STAT1 activation requires phosphorylation/dimerization/nuclear translocation; GPI or Pygl siRNA decreased STAT1-Y701 phosphorylation and nuclear import, reversed by added UDPG. Glucose is the glucopyranose donor, not the previously attached furanose isomer. Macrophage immune-signaling mechanism; no direct hepatic outcome is inferred. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Disruption of glycogenolysis by either GPI or Pygl siRNA markedly inhibited the phosphorylation of STAT1 at Tyr701 and its nuclear translocation, which could be reversed by the addition of UDPG. UDPG also induced STAT1 phosphorylation.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: biological_model_context=human hepatocytes (in vitro study); cell uptake of mipomersen sodium demonstrated (cell-associated concentrations 164–909 µg/g)
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=viability_or_cell_number | assay_and_readout=hepatocyte viability expressed as percent of viable cells relative to vehicle-treated cells
new_or_changed_cards.reported_value: result_value=viability 88.0%–106% of vehicle; no cytotoxicity at tested concentrations
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: concentration_values=8–800 | concentration_unit=ug_per_ml | extra_details=Focal molecule mipomersen sodium. No cytotoxicity observed at tested concentrations up to 800 µg/mL. Cells treated with vehicle alone were the comparator. Dosing concentrations for cell uptake assessment were 8–800 µg/mL. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In the in vitro CYP inhibition / cytotoxicity evaluation, the viability of human hepatocytes treated with mipomersen sodium ranged from 88.0% to 106% of the viability of cells treated with vehicle alone, and mipomersen sodium exhibited no cytotoxicity at the tested concentrations. Cell-associated concentrations of mipomersen sodium were 164–909 µg/g at dosing concentrations of 8–800 µg/mL.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: biological_model_context=Cryopreserved human hepatocytes; in-vitro assay used concurrently for CYP isoenzyme activity evaluation (CYP1A2, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, CYP3A4) and cell-associated uptake measurement | culture_format=2d_planar
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=viability_or_cell_number | assay_and_readout=Cytotoxicity assessment in cryopreserved human hepatocytes—qualitative outcome
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: extra_details=Focal molecule is mipomersen sodium (ISIS 301012), a 20-mer phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotide targeting human apoB-100 mRNA. Cytotoxicity result is qualitative with no numeric potency, assay readout, exposure duration, or vehicle concentration reported in the provided text; the 800 µg/mL (~100 µmol/L) top concentration and <10% CYP inhibition are reported for the enzyme-activity evaluation, which is a CYP assay without a concurrent hepatocyte health/reserve endpoint and is therefore not extracted as an eligible hepatocyte phenotype. No quantitative or regimen details for the cytotoxicity assessment were supplied in the text window. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In the in-vitro evaluation in cryopreserved human hepatocytes, mipomersen sodium was tested and exhibited no cytotoxicity. The same in-vitro study showed significant cell uptake by analysing cell-associated concentrations of mipomersen sodium, and all evaluated CYP enzyme activities had <10% inhibition at tested concentrations up to 800 µg/mL (~100 µmol/L) of mipomersen sodium.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: assay_format=imaging_or_morphometry | biological_system_context=Cryopreserved human primary hepatocytes (cryoheps, lot HC3-30), sandwich-cultured in Long-Term medium for 10 d from the next day after seeding and then in CDI maintenance medium (CM medium) for 5 d; intrinsically metabolically competent primary hepatocytes.
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: assay_category=canalicular_morphology_or_dynamics | endpoint_metric=bile canalicular length and average canalicular area per image (anti-BSEP stained)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: tested_entity_form=parent | probe_or_analyte=bile canaliculi (CDFDFA fluorescence and anti-BSEP immunostaining) | exposure_conditions=2',5'-Dideoxyadenosine (AMPK inhibitor) added during the 5 d culture on the CM medium; test concentration not reported in the extracted text. | extra_details=2',5'-Dideoxyadenosine is described in the paper as an AMP inhibitor. Test rationale: taurocholate activates AMPK and extends bile canaliculi (Fu et al. 2011, cited). Canalicular readout by CDFDA assay and immunostaining; bar graph gives average area of each bile canaliculus stained by anti-BSEP, means ± SD (n=3). The paper did not report a numeric area/length value. The original article calls 2-prime,5-prime-dideoxyadenosine an AMPK inhibitor. This is source terminology; the canalicular phenotype alone does not validate a direct or selective AMPK target mechanism. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Because taurocholate activates AMPK and extends the bile canaliculi (Fu et al. 2011), the effect on bile canaliculi formation was examined by adding 2',5'-dideoxyadenosine, an AMPK inhibitor, to the CM medium. This shortened the length of the bile canaliculi (Fig. 6d and e). The canaliculi were observed using the CDFDA assay and by immunostaining, and the bar graph shows the average area of each bile canaliculus stained by anti-BSEP, presented as means ± SD (n=3).

new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: assay_family=targeted_gene_expression | endpoint_and_comparator=HBV DNA copy reduction (percent decrease) in 5-AZA-reprogrammed REP-HepG2-NTCP cells vs untreated (non-IFNα) cells after IFNα treatment
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: molecule_dose_value=2 | molecule_dose_unit=µM | immune_stimulus_regimen=HBV infection at MOI 100 (with PEG 8000) for 24 h, followed by IFNα 10,000 IU/mL | exposure_schedule=5-AZA 2 µM for 10 days (reprogramming), then HBV infection (MOI 100, 24 h), then IFNα 10,000 IU/mL every 3 days for 9 days before total DNA collection | extra_details=Mean ± SD = 63.97% ± 0.07%; p < 0.0001 (t test). | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: REP-HepG2-NTCP cells were infected with HBV using PEG 8000 at an MOI of 100 for 24 h after the reprogramming procedure, and HBV DNA copies were reduced by 63.97% ± 0.07% in response to 10,000 IU/mL IFNα for 9 days (p < 0.0001, t test).

new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: clinical_phenotype=acute_hepatitis
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: agent_type=small_molecule_or_chemical | liver_injury_identifier=UMLS:C0267797 | qualifying_conditions=The paper notes adverse hepatic reactions may occur more commonly in elderly patients with malignant disease treated with prolonged high doses; continuing the drug during the prodrome greatly increases severity and mortality. | extra_details=Latency about 2-3 months; prodromal non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) for 1-4 weeks before jaundice. Mechanism uncertain, may be direct but more likely idiosyncratic via a metabolite; immunologic mechanism not excluded. Used in antiandrogenic conditions, recommended dose 2-300 mg daily (Androcur, Cyprostat). Figure shows serum total bilirubin and aspartate aminotransferase from withdrawal (day 0) to normalization of liver function tests; liver function monitoring recommended. Isoniazid and methyldopa mentioned only as analogous hepatotoxic drugs, not attributed as culprits in this case. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: This case describes drug-induced acute hepatitis caused by cyproterone acetate, with features similar to acute hepatitis from isoniazid and methyldopa: after about two to three months of treatment, non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) develop for one to four weeks before the onset of jaundice; severity and mortality increase greatly if the drug is continued during the prodrome. The toxicity of cyproterone acetate may be direct but is more likely the result of an idiosyncratic reaction caused by one of its metabolites, and an immunological mechanism has not been excluded.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: The authors identify cyproterone as the cause of fulminant hepatitis in a patient, stating the Naranjo probability scale indicates a probable drug-related event because liver function tests were normal before drug administration. The temporal relationship between cyproterone administration and acute liver failure is described as clear with no alternative cause.

new_or_changed_cards.reported_value: result_value=circumvented kinase-dead LKB1-mediated inhibition of canalicular network formation (canalicular formation restored)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: extra_details=Focal molecule AICAR acts as an AMPK activator. Kinase-dead LKB1 construct alone inhibited canalicular network formation; AICAR circumvented this inhibition, indicating direct AMPK action on canalicular formation. Original paper uses the membrane-permeable riboside; intracellular phosphorylation forms the distinct ZMP metabolite. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes, AICAR, which activates AMPK, circumvented the inhibitory effect of kinase-dead LKB1 constructs on canalicular network formation. Canalicular network formation was assessed by immunostaining for the apical protein ABCB1 and the tight junction marker occludin. Because AICAR restored canalicular formation despite kinase-dead LKB1, the authors conclude AMPK directly affects canalicular network formation.

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: agent_type=small_molecule_or_chemical | liver_injury_identifier=UMLS:C0267797 | qualifying_conditions=The paper notes adverse hepatic reactions may occur more commonly in elderly patients with malignant disease treated with prolonged high doses; continuing the drug during the prodrome greatly increases severity and mortality. | extra_details=Latency about 2-3 months; prodromal non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) for 1-4 weeks before jaundice. Mechanism uncertain, may be direct but more likely idiosyncratic via a metabolite; immunologic mechanism not excluded. Used in antiandrogenic conditions, recommended dose 2-300 mg daily (Androcur, Cyprostat). Figure shows serum total bilirubin and aspartate aminotransferase from withdrawal (day 0) to normalization of liver function tests; liver function monitoring recommended. Isoniazid and methyldopa mentioned only as analogous hepatotoxic drugs, not attributed as culprits in this case. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: This case describes drug-induced acute hepatitis caused by cyproterone acetate, with features similar to acute hepatitis from isoniazid and methyldopa: after about two to three months of treatment, non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) develop for one to four weeks before the onset of jaundice; severity and mortality increase greatly if the drug is continued during the prodrome. The toxicity of cyproterone acetate may be direct but is more likely the result of an idiosyncratic reaction caused by one of its metabolites, and an immunological mechanism has not been excluded.

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: agent_type=small_molecule_or_chemical | liver_injury_identifier=UMLS:C0267797 | qualifying_conditions=The paper notes adverse hepatic reactions may occur more commonly in elderly patients with malignant disease treated with prolonged high doses; continuing the drug during the prodrome greatly increases severity and mortality. | extra_details=Latency about 2-3 months; prodromal non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) for 1-4 weeks before jaundice. Mechanism uncertain, may be direct but more likely idiosyncratic via a metabolite; immunologic mechanism not excluded. Used in antiandrogenic conditions, recommended dose 2-300 mg daily (Androcur, Cyprostat). Figure shows serum total bilirubin and aspartate aminotransferase from withdrawal (day 0) to normalization of liver function tests; liver function monitoring recommended. Isoniazid and methyldopa mentioned only as analogous hepatotoxic drugs, not attributed as culprits in this case. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: This case describes drug-induced acute hepatitis caused by cyproterone acetate, with features similar to acute hepatitis from isoniazid and methyldopa: after about two to three months of treatment, non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) develop for one to four weeks before the onset of jaundice; severity and mortality increase greatly if the drug is continued during the prodrome. The toxicity of cyproterone acetate may be direct but is more likely the result of an idiosyncratic reaction caused by one of its metabolites, and an immunological mechanism has not been excluded.

Used in antiandrogenic conditions, recommended dose 2-300 mg daily (Androcur, Cyprostat). Figure shows serum total bilirubin and aspartate aminotransferase from withdrawal (day 0) to normalization of liver function tests; liver function monitoring recommended. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: This case describes drug-induced acute hepatitis caused by cyproterone acetate, with features similar to acute hepatitis from isoniazid and methyldopa: after about two to three months of treatment, non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) develop for one to four weeks before the onset of jaundice; severity and mortality increase greatly if the drug is continued during the prodrome. The toxicity of cyproterone acetate may be direct but is more likely the result of an idiosyncratic reaction caused by one of its metabolites, and an immunological mechanism has not been excluded.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: To confirm that ROS contributes to azacytidine-induced cell necrosis, an Image-iT LIVE Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) Kit was used to detect ROS in untreated and azacytidine-treated U266 myeloma cells. Cells were labeled with carboxy-H2DCFDA, which fluoresces when oxidized by ROS, and nuclei were stained with blue-fluorescent Hoechst 33342. The azacytidine-treated cells exhibited much stronger green fluorescence (Figure 2e) compared to untreated cells (Figure 2d), indicating that azacytidine induced a significant increase in ROS.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: To confirm that ROS contributes to azacytidine-induced cell necrosis, an Image-iT LIVE Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) Kit was used to detect ROS in untreated and azacytidine-treated U266 myeloma cells. Azacytidine exposure also showed concentration-dependent necrosis (22% necrotic cells at 5 μM, 38% at 80 μM, 24 h), supporting the oxidative-stress link. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: To confirm that ROS contributes to azacytidine-induced cell necrosis, an Image-iT LIVE Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) Kit was used to detect ROS in untreated and azacytidine-treated U266 myeloma cells. Cells were labeled with carboxy-H2DCFDA, which fluoresces when oxidized by ROS, and nuclei were stained with blue-fluorescent Hoechst 33342. The azacytidine-treated cells exhibited much stronger green fluorescence (Figure 2e) compared to untreated cells (Figure 2d), indicating that azacytidine induced a significant increase in ROS.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: biological_model_context=Collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes expressing a kinase-dead LKB1 (dominant-negative) construct | culture_format=2d_planar
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=morphology_polarity_or_canalicular_structure | assay_and_readout=Immunofluorescence of apical protein ABCB1 and tight junction marker occludin (with bright-field illumination)—canalicular network formation
new_or_changed_cards.reported_value: result_value=circumvented kinase-dead LKB1-mediated inhibition of canalicular network formation (canalicular formation restored)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: extra_details=Focal molecule AICAR acts as an AMPK activator. Kinase-dead LKB1 construct alone inhibited canalicular network formation; AICAR circumvented this inhibition, indicating direct AMPK action on canalicular formation. Original paper uses the membrane-permeable riboside; intracellular phosphorylation forms the distinct ZMP metabolite. Correct the unrelated phosphorylated heterocycle without changing protective or negative findings. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes, AICAR, which activates AMPK, circumvented the inhibitory effect of kinase-dead LKB1 constructs on canalicular network formation. Canalicular network formation was assessed by immunostaining for the apical protein ABCB1 and the tight junction marker occludin. Because AICAR restored canalicular formation despite kinase-dead LKB1, the authors conclude AMPK directly affects canalicular network formation.

new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=other_hepatocyte_function_or_reserve | assay_and_readout=RT-qPCR—mRNA levels of hepatocyte differentiation markers ALB, SLC10A1, CYP3A4, and miR-122 in reconditioned versus control HCC cells
new_or_changed_cards.reported_value: result_value=increased—ALB, SLC10A1, CYP3A4, and miR-122 significantly induced, indicating restored hepatic differentiation; no ALB induction in Hep3B (already elevated ~7.5-fold in non-reconditioned Hep3B versus HepG2)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: concentration_values=2 | concentration_unit=umol_per_l | exposure_duration_and_schedule=reconditioning exposure to 2 uM 5-AZA for 12 days; total RNA extracted after 3 and 5 days of culture without 5-AZA (T1 and T2) | exposure_regimen=repeated_dose_with_recovery | extra_details=Phenotype named: restoration of hepatocyte differentiation markers (differentiated-function/reserve endpoint). Non-reconditioned HCC cells were used as controls. CYP1A2, TAT, G6Pc, and HNF4A mRNAs also upregulated in reconditioned cells; CDH1 augmented; AFP downregulated. Exposure regimen classified as repeated_dose_with_recovery because cells were cultured without 5-AZA (3 and 5 days) before RNA assessment. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: We analyzed the expression of a cluster of characteristic hepatospecific genes: albumin (ALB), solute carrier family 10 member 1 (SLC10A1), cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4, and microRNA-122 (miR-122). After epigenetic reconditioning of HepG2 and Hep3B cells with 2 μM 5-AZA for 12 days, qRT-PCR data revealed that these genes were significantly induced, indicating a restoration of hepatic differentiation in the reconditioned HCC cells. miR-122 levels were strongly increased in the reconditioned cells (p < 0.001); there was an apparent absence of ALB induction in reconditioned Hep3B cells, but ALB was already elevated in non-reconditioned Hep3B cells.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: We analyzed the expression of a cluster of characteristic hepatospecific genes: albumin (ALB), solute carrier family 10 member 1 (SLC10A1), cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4, and microRNA-122 (miR-122). After epigenetic reconditioning of HepG2 and Hep3B cells with 2 μM 5-AZA for 12 days, qRT-PCR data revealed that these genes were significantly induced, indicating a restoration of hepatic differentiation in the reconditioned HCC cells. miR-122 levels were strongly increased in the reconditioned cells (p < 0.001); there was an apparent absence of ALB induction in reconditioned Hep3B cells, but ALB was already elevated in non-reconditioned Hep3B cells.

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: treatment_and_comparator_context=Azacytidine treatment for 24 h, compared to untreated cells (no concentration explicitly stated for the ROS assay images) | extra_details=Result reported qualitatively as much stronger green fluorescence in azacytidine-treated cells compared to untreated; nuclei counterstained with Hoechst 33342 (DAPI listed in entity list as Hoechst 33342 synonym is a text discrepancy). new_or_changed_cards.support_text: To confirm that ROS contributes to azacytidine-induced cell necrosis, an Image-iT LIVE Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) Kit was used to detect ROS in untreated and azacytidine-treated U266 myeloma cells. Cells were labeled with carboxy-H2DCFDA, which fluoresces when oxidized by ROS, and nuclei were stained with blue-fluorescent Hoechst 33342. The azacytidine-treated cells exhibited much stronger green fluorescence (Figure 2e) compared to untreated cells (Figure 2d), indicating that azacytidine induced a significant increase in ROS.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: This case describes drug-induced acute hepatitis caused by cyproterone acetate, with features similar to acute hepatitis from isoniazid and methyldopa: after about two to three months of treatment, non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) develop for one to four weeks before the onset of jaundice; severity and mortality increase greatly if the drug is continued during the prodrome. The toxicity of cyproterone acetate may be direct but is more likely the result of an idiosyncratic reaction caused by one of its metabolites, and an immunological mechanism has not been excluded.

new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=other_hepatocyte_function_or_reserve | assay_and_readout=RT-qPCR—mRNA levels of hepatocyte differentiation markers ALB, SLC10A1, CYP3A4, and miR-122 in reconditioned versus control HCC cells
new_or_changed_cards.reported_value: result_value=increased—ALB, SLC10A1, CYP3A4, and miR-122 significantly induced, indicating restored hepatic differentiation; no ALB induction in Hep3B (already elevated ~7.5-fold in non-reconditioned Hep3B versus HepG2)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: concentration_values=2 | concentration_unit=umol_per_l | exposure_duration_and_schedule=reconditioning exposure to 2 uM 5-AZA for 12 days; total RNA extracted after 3 and 5 days of culture without 5-AZA (T1 and T2) | exposure_regimen=repeated_dose_with_recovery | extra_details=Phenotype named: restoration of hepatocyte differentiation markers (differentiated-function/reserve endpoint). Non-reconditioned HCC cells were used as controls. CYP1A2, TAT, G6Pc, and HNF4A mRNAs also upregulated in reconditioned cells; CDH1 augmented; AFP downregulated. Exposure regimen classified as repeated_dose_with_recovery because cells were cultured without 5-AZA (3 and 5 days) before RNA assessment. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: We analyzed the expression of a cluster of characteristic hepatospecific genes: albumin (ALB), solute carrier family 10 member 1 (SLC10A1), cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4, and microRNA-122 (miR-122). After epigenetic reconditioning of HepG2 and Hep3B cells with 2 μM 5-AZA for 12 days, qRT-PCR data revealed that these genes were significantly induced, indicating a restoration of hepatic differentiation in the reconditioned HCC cells. miR-122 levels were strongly increased in the reconditioned cells (p < 0.001); there was an apparent absence of ALB induction in reconditioned Hep3B cells, but ALB was already elevated in non-reconditioned Hep3B cells.

The paper describes endoplasmin as functioning in ER processing/transport of secreted proteins and possessing ATPase and calcium-binding properties.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: biological_model_context=U266 myeloma cell line; Homo sapiens | assay_and_platform=Image-iT LIVE Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) Kit with carboxy-H2DCFDA probe; fluorescence microscopy with Hoechst 33342 nuclear counterstain
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_class=reactive_species | endpoint_name=total reactive oxygen species (carboxy-H2DCFDA oxidation)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: treatment_and_comparator_context=Azacytidine treatment for 24 h, compared to untreated cells (no concentration explicitly stated for the ROS assay images) | extra_details=Result reported qualitatively as much stronger green fluorescence in azacytidine-treated cells compared to untreated; nuclei counterstained with Hoechst 33342 (DAPI listed in entity list as Hoechst 33342 synonym is a text discrepancy). Azacytidine exposure also showed concentration-dependent necrosis (22% necrotic cells at 5 μM, 38% at 80 μM, 24 h), supporting the oxidative-stress link. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: To confirm that ROS contributes to azacytidine-induced cell necrosis, an Image-iT LIVE Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) Kit was used to detect ROS in untreated and azacytidine-treated U266 myeloma cells. Cells were labeled with carboxy-H2DCFDA, which fluoresces when oxidized by ROS, and nuclei were stained with blue-fluorescent Hoechst 33342. The azacytidine-treated cells exhibited much stronger green fluorescence (Figure 2e) compared to untreated cells (Figure 2d), indicating that azacytidine induced a significant increase in ROS.

new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: assay_family=transcriptomics | endpoint_and_comparator=Cholestasis-association gene-expression signature (PC1 value) for CPA-treated rats versus control; CPA showed a low PC1 value and was not separated from controls by PCA despite being reported to induce cholestasis.
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: exposure_schedule=In vivo rat administration of CPA (single dose); gene expression sampled at 24 h after single dosage. | extra_details=CPA (CpA) did not separate by PCA in the cholestasis classification, attributed to lack of hepatocyte bile-acid cytotoxicity; cited prior work observed increased plasma bile salt after 10 mg/kg CPA in rats and suggested inhibition of bile-acid uptake from portal blood, with no change in liver histology. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: CPA is reported to induce cholestasis, but showed a low PC1 value in the current study. It was suggested that CPA inhibits the uptake of bile acids from portal blood into hepatocytes, and there was no change in liver histology, so the drug was not separated by PCA in the current study.

new_or_changed_cards.reported_value: result_value=increased—ALB, SLC10A1, CYP3A4, and miR-122 significantly induced, indicating restored hepatic differentiation; no ALB induction in Hep3B (already elevated ~7.5-fold in non-reconditioned Hep3B versus HepG2)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: concentration_values=2 | concentration_unit=umol_per_l | exposure_duration_and_schedule=reconditioning exposure to 2 uM 5-AZA for 12 days; total RNA extracted after 3 and 5 days of culture without 5-AZA (T1 and T2) | exposure_regimen=repeated_dose_with_recovery | extra_details=Phenotype named: restoration of hepatocyte differentiation markers (differentiated-function/reserve endpoint). new_or_changed_cards.support_text: We analyzed the expression of a cluster of characteristic hepatospecific genes: albumin (ALB), solute carrier family 10 member 1 (SLC10A1), cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4, and microRNA-122 (miR-122). After epigenetic reconditioning of HepG2 and Hep3B cells with 2 μM 5-AZA for 12 days, qRT-PCR data revealed that these genes were significantly induced, indicating a restoration of hepatic differentiation in the reconditioned HCC cells. miR-122 levels were strongly increased in the reconditioned cells (p < 0.001); there was an apparent absence of ALB induction in reconditioned Hep3B cells, but ALB was already elevated in non-reconditioned Hep3B cells.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: biological_model_context=U266 myeloma cell line; Homo sapiens | assay_and_platform=Image-iT LIVE Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) Kit with carboxy-H2DCFDA probe; fluorescence microscopy with Hoechst 33342 nuclear counterstain

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: treatment_and_comparator_context=Azacytidine treatment for 24 h, compared to untreated cells (no concentration explicitly stated for the ROS assay images) | extra_details=Result reported qualitatively as much stronger green fluorescence in azacytidine-treated cells compared to untreated; nuclei counterstained with Hoechst 33342 (DAPI listed in entity list as Hoechst 33342 synonym is a text discrepancy). Azacytidine exposure also showed concentration-dependent necrosis (22% necrotic cells at 5 μM, 38% at 80 μM, 24 h), supporting the oxidative-stress link. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: To confirm that ROS contributes to azacytidine-induced cell necrosis, an Image-iT LIVE Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) Kit was used to detect ROS in untreated and azacytidine-treated U266 myeloma cells. Cells were labeled with carboxy-H2DCFDA, which fluoresces when oxidized by ROS, and nuclei were stained with blue-fluorescent Hoechst 33342. The azacytidine-treated cells exhibited much stronger green fluorescence (Figure 2e) compared to untreated cells (Figure 2d), indicating that azacytidine induced a significant increase in ROS.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: To confirm that ROS contributes to azacytidine-induced cell necrosis, an Image-iT LIVE Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) Kit was used to detect ROS in untreated and azacytidine-treated U266 myeloma cells. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: This case describes drug-induced acute hepatitis caused by cyproterone acetate, with features similar to acute hepatitis from isoniazid and methyldopa: after about two to three months of treatment, non-specific symptoms (gastrointestinal upset, malaise, muscle weakness) develop for one to four weeks before the onset of jaundice; severity and mortality increase greatly if the drug is continued during the prodrome. The toxicity of cyproterone acetate may be direct but is more likely the result of an idiosyncratic reaction caused by one of its metabolites, and an immunological mechanism has not been excluded.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Guanosine prevents ROS production elicited by OGD in cortical astrocytic cells. Astrocytes were subjected to 2.5 h of oxygen and glucose deprivation (OGD) followed by 24 h of reperfusion with culture medium (control) or with guanosine (OGD GUO, 10 µM). ROS production was evaluated by DCF fluorescence emission assay and expressed as fold increase from control (incubated for 24 h in physiological culture medium). Data are means ± S.E.M. from 4 to 5 different cell batches; #p < 0.05 represents means significantly different from the OGD group (ANOVA followed by Tukey's test). The OGD-induced increase in ROS was reduced by guanosine treatment.

new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_class=reactive_species | endpoint_name=cellular ROS levels (DCFH oxidation)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: exposure_level=100 µM | exposure_unit=µM | treatment_and_comparator_context=Pre-treated for 1 h with 100 µM guanosine, followed by addition of 5 mM azide for 3 h; comparator azide alone; HO1 inhibitor ZnPP IX (10 µM) abolished the guanosine effect; guanosine had no effect on the control condition | extra_details=Azide alone increased ROS to 155 ± 10% of control (~55% increase); guanosine value 99 ± 7%, *p < 0.01. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: ROS levels (measured by DCFH oxidation) increased 55% after azide exposure. Guanosine had no effect on the control condition.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: biological_model_context=cultured cortical astrocytic cells; in vitro OGD ischemia model | assay_and_platform=DCF fluorescence emission assay; fluorescence (fold increase from control)
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_class=reactive_species | endpoint_name=ROS production (DCF fluorescence)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: exposure_level=10 µM | exposure_unit=µM | treatment_and_comparator_context=2.5 h OGD followed by 24 h reperfusion with guanosine 10 µM in culture medium; compared with OGD group reperfused with culture medium alone (control = 24 h physiological medium) | extra_details=ROS expressed as fold increase from control, but no numeric value given in text; data are means ± S.E.M. from 4-5 different cell batches; #p<0.05 vs OGD group (ANOVA, Tukey's test). In separate experiments, the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 (10 µM) partially blocked the guanosine-induced decrease in ROS, while PD98059 (10 µM, MEK) and chelerythrine (1 µM, PKC) did not alter the decrease. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Guanosine prevents ROS production elicited by OGD in cortical astrocytic cells. Astrocytes were subjected to 2.5 h of oxygen and glucose deprivation (OGD) followed by 24 h of reperfusion with culture medium (control) or with guanosine (OGD GUO, 10 µM). ROS production was evaluated by DCF fluorescence emission assay and expressed as fold increase from control (incubated for 24 h in physiological culture medium). Data are means ± S.E.M. from 4 to 5 different cell batches; #p < 0.05 represents means significantly different from the OGD group (ANOVA followed by Tukey's test). The OGD-induced increase in ROS was reduced by guanosine treatment.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: biological_model_context=Cryopreserved human hepatocytes; in-vitro assay used concurrently for CYP isoenzyme activity evaluation (CYP1A2, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, CYP3A4) and cell-associated uptake measurement | culture_format=2d_planar

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: extra_details=Focal molecule is mipomersen sodium (ISIS 301012), a 20-mer phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotide targeting human apoB-100 mRNA. Cytotoxicity result is qualitative with no numeric potency, assay readout, exposure duration, or vehicle concentration reported in the provided text; the 800 µg/mL (~100 µmol/L) top concentration and <10% CYP inhibition are reported for the enzyme-activity evaluation, which is a CYP assay without a concurrent hepatocyte health/reserve endpoint and is therefore not extracted as an eligible hepatocyte phenotype. No quantitative or regimen details for the cytotoxicity assessment were supplied in the text window. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In the in-vitro evaluation in cryopreserved human hepatocytes, mipomersen sodium was tested and exhibited no cytotoxicity. The same in-vitro study showed significant cell uptake by analysing cell-associated concentrations of mipomersen sodium, and all evaluated CYP enzyme activities had <10% inhibition at tested concentrations up to 800 µg/mL (~100 µmol/L) of mipomersen sodium.

new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=morphology_polarity_or_canalicular_structure | assay_and_readout=Immunofluorescence of apical protein ABCB1 and tight junction marker occludin (with bright-field illumination)—canalicular network formation
new_or_changed_cards.reported_value: result_value=circumvented kinase-dead LKB1-mediated inhibition of canalicular network formation (canalicular formation restored)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: extra_details=Focal molecule AICAR acts as an AMPK activator. Kinase-dead LKB1 construct alone inhibited canalicular network formation; AICAR circumvented this inhibition, indicating direct AMPK action on canalicular formation. Original paper uses the membrane-permeable riboside; intracellular phosphorylation forms the distinct ZMP metabolite. Correct the unrelated phosphorylated heterocycle without changing protective or negative findings. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes, AICAR, which activates AMPK, circumvented the inhibitory effect of kinase-dead LKB1 constructs on canalicular network formation. Canalicular network formation was assessed by immunostaining for the apical protein ABCB1 and the tight junction marker occludin. Because AICAR restored canalicular formation despite kinase-dead LKB1, the authors conclude AMPK directly affects canalicular network formation.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: biological_model_context=Collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes expressing a kinase-dead LKB1 (dominant-negative) construct | culture_format=2d_planar
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=morphology_polarity_or_canalicular_structure | assay_and_readout=Immunofluorescence of apical protein ABCB1 and tight junction marker occludin (with bright-field illumination)—canalicular network formation
new_or_changed_cards.reported_value: result_value=circumvented kinase-dead LKB1-mediated inhibition of canalicular network formation (canalicular formation restored)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: extra_details=Focal molecule AICAR acts as an AMPK activator. Kinase-dead LKB1 construct alone inhibited canalicular network formation; AICAR circumvented this inhibition, indicating direct AMPK action on canalicular formation. Original paper uses the membrane-permeable riboside; intracellular phosphorylation forms the distinct ZMP metabolite. Correct the unrelated phosphorylated heterocycle without changing protective or negative findings. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes, AICAR, which activates AMPK, circumvented the inhibitory effect of kinase-dead LKB1 constructs on canalicular network formation. Canalicular network formation was assessed by immunostaining for the apical protein ABCB1 and the tight junction marker occludin. Because AICAR restored canalicular formation despite kinase-dead LKB1, the authors conclude AMPK directly affects canalicular network formation.

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: exposure_level=100 µM | exposure_unit=µM | treatment_and_comparator_context=Pre-treated for 1 h with 100 µM guanosine, followed by addition of 5 mM azide for 3 h; comparator azide alone; HO1 inhibitor ZnPP IX (10 µM) abolished the guanosine effect; guanosine had no effect on the control condition | extra_details=Azide alone increased ROS to 155 ± 10% of control (~55% increase); guanosine value 99 ± 7%, *p < 0.01. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: ROS levels (measured by DCFH oxidation) increased 55% after azide exposure. Guanosine prevented this effect, decreasing the ROS levels from 155 ± 10% to 99 ± 7% (*p* < 0.01). The HO1 inhibitor ZnPP IX (10 µM) abolished the guanosine effect. Guanosine had no effect on the control condition.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: biological_model_context=cultured cortical astrocytic cells; in vitro OGD ischemia model | assay_and_platform=DCF fluorescence emission assay; fluorescence (fold increase from control)
new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_class=reactive_species | endpoint_name=ROS production (DCF fluorescence)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: exposure_level=10 µM | exposure_unit=µM | treatment_and_comparator_context=2.5 h OGD followed by 24 h reperfusion with guanosine 10 µM in culture medium; compared with OGD group reperfused with culture medium alone (control = 24 h physiological medium) | extra_details=ROS expressed as fold increase from control, but no numeric value given in text; data are means ± S.E.M. from 4-5 different cell batches; #p<0.05 vs OGD group (ANOVA, Tukey's test). In separate experiments, the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 (10 µM) partially blocked the guanosine-induced decrease in ROS, while PD98059 (10 µM, MEK) and chelerythrine (1 µM, PKC) did not alter the decrease. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Guanosine prevents ROS production elicited by OGD in cortical astrocytic cells. Astrocytes were subjected to 2.5 h of oxygen and glucose deprivation (OGD) followed by 24 h of reperfusion with culture medium (control) or with guanosine (OGD GUO, 10 µM). ROS production was evaluated by DCF fluorescence emission assay and expressed as fold increase from control (incubated for 24 h in physiological culture medium). Data are means ± S.E.M. from 4 to 5 different cell batches; #p < 0.05 represents means significantly different from the OGD group (ANOVA followed by Tukey's test). The OGD-induced increase in ROS was reduced by guanosine treatment.

new_or_changed_cards.assay_context: biological_model_context=Cryopreserved human hepatocytes; in-vitro assay used concurrently for CYP isoenzyme activity evaluation (CYP1A2, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, CYP3A4) and cell-associated uptake measurement | culture_format=2d_planar

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: extra_details=Focal molecule is mipomersen sodium (ISIS 301012), a 20-mer phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotide targeting human apoB-100 mRNA. new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: exposure_level=10 µM | exposure_unit=µM | treatment_and_comparator_context=2.5 h OGD followed by 24 h reperfusion with guanosine 10 µM in culture medium; compared with OGD group reperfused with culture medium alone (control = 24 h physiological medium) | extra_details=ROS expressed as fold increase from control, but no numeric value given in text; data are means ± S.E.M. from 4-5 different cell batches; #p<0.05 vs OGD group (ANOVA, Tukey's test). new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Guanosine prevents ROS production elicited by OGD in cortical astrocytic cells. Astrocytes were subjected to 2.5 h of oxygen and glucose deprivation (OGD) followed by 24 h of reperfusion with culture medium (control) or with guanosine (OGD GUO, 10 µM). ROS production was evaluated by DCF fluorescence emission assay and expressed as fold increase from control (incubated for 24 h in physiological culture medium). Data are means ± S.E.M. from 4 to 5 different cell batches; #p < 0.05 represents means significantly different from the OGD group (ANOVA followed by Tukey's test). The OGD-induced increase in ROS was reduced by guanosine treatment.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes, AICAR, which activates AMPK, circumvented the inhibitory effect of kinase-dead LKB1 constructs on canalicular network formation. Because AICAR restored canalicular formation despite kinase-dead LKB1, the authors conclude AMPK directly affects canalicular network formation.

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: exposure_level=10 µM | exposure_unit=µM | treatment_and_comparator_context=2.5 h OGD followed by 24 h reperfusion with guanosine 10 µM in culture medium; compared with OGD group reperfused with culture medium alone (control = 24 h physiological medium) | extra_details=ROS expressed as fold increase from control, but no numeric value given in text; data are means ± S.E.M. from 4-5 different cell batches; #p<0.05 vs OGD group (ANOVA, Tukey's test). In separate experiments, the PI3K inhibitor LY294002 (10 µM) partially blocked the guanosine-induced decrease in ROS, while PD98059 (10 µM, MEK) and chelerythrine (1 µM, PKC) did not alter the decrease. | needs_more_context=False
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Guanosine prevents ROS production elicited by OGD in cortical astrocytic cells. Astrocytes were subjected to 2.5 h of oxygen and glucose deprivation (OGD) followed by 24 h of reperfusion with culture medium (control) or with guanosine (OGD GUO, 10 µM). ROS production was evaluated by DCF fluorescence emission assay and expressed as fold increase from control (incubated for 24 h in physiological culture medium). Data are means ± S.E.M. from 4 to 5 different cell batches; #p < 0.05 represents means significantly different from the OGD group (ANOVA followed by Tukey's test). The OGD-induced increase in ROS was reduced by guanosine treatment.

new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: extra_details=Focal molecule is mipomersen sodium (ISIS 301012), a 20-mer phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotide targeting human apoB-100 mRNA. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In the in-vitro evaluation in cryopreserved human hepatocytes, mipomersen sodium was tested and exhibited no cytotoxicity. new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=morphology_polarity_or_canalicular_structure | assay_and_readout=Immunofluorescence of apical protein ABCB1 and tight junction marker occludin (with bright-field illumination)—canalicular network formation
new_or_changed_cards.reported_value: result_value=circumvented kinase-dead LKB1-mediated inhibition of canalicular network formation (canalicular formation restored)
new_or_changed_cards.qualifying_conditions: extra_details=Focal molecule AICAR acts as an AMPK activator. Kinase-dead LKB1 construct alone inhibited canalicular network formation; AICAR circumvented this inhibition, indicating direct AMPK action on canalicular formation. Original paper uses the membrane-permeable riboside; intracellular phosphorylation forms the distinct ZMP metabolite. Correct the unrelated phosphorylated heterocycle without changing protective or negative findings. | needs_more_context=True
new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes, AICAR, which activates AMPK, circumvented the inhibitory effect of kinase-dead LKB1 constructs on canalicular network formation. Canalicular network formation was assessed by immunostaining for the apical protein ABCB1 and the tight junction marker occludin. Because AICAR restored canalicular formation despite kinase-dead LKB1, the authors conclude AMPK directly affects canalicular network formation.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Because cytotoxicity involves mitochondrial impairment by the respiratory processes and subsequent depletion of cellular energy supplies in the form of ATP, the authors monitored cellular ATP levels and some mitochondrial physiological functions (Figs 1, 3 and 4; Tables 1 and 2) and found mitochondria to be a primary target when isolated hepatocytes are exposed to OPP or its metabolites. In isolated mitochondria, the order of potency for respiration or Ca2+ release was PBQ > OPP > PHQ, so the parent compound itself has an inhibitory action on mitochondrial function.

new_or_changed_cards.support_text: Rats dosed with N-hydroxy-benzylamine HCl excreted a GSH conjugate (M12, S-benzyl-L-glutathione, MH+ at m/z 427). SIM studies suggested this metabolite accounted for less than 10% of the administered dose. The MS/MS spectrum showed fragments at m/z 352, 298, 265 (base peak), and 177, and the structure was confirmed by comparison with an authentic synthetic standard. The conjugate forms via the hydroxylamine and nitroso intermediates. M1 and benzylamine were the major metabolites accounting for greater than 90% of the administered dose. None of the GSH adducts previously identified in benzylamine-dosed rats were found in the bile of N-hydroxyl benzylamine-dosed animals.

new_or_changed_cards.endpoint: endpoint_category=morphology_polarity_or_canalicular_structure | assay_and_readout=Immunofluorescence of apical protein ABCB1 and tight junction marker occludin (with bright-field illumination)—canalicular network formation

Kinase-dead LKB1 construct alone inhibited canalicular network formation; AICAR circumvented this inhibition, indicating direct AMPK action on canalicular formation. new_or_changed_cards.support_text: In collagen sandwich cultures of rat primary hepatocytes, AICAR, which activates AMPK, circumvented the inhibitory effect of kinase-dead LKB1 constructs on canalicular network formation. Because AICAR restored canalicular formation despite kinase-dead LKB1, the authors conclude AMPK directly affects canalicular network formation.
